guideline: Radiologists annotated error counts per category for generated reports; metrics are evaluated based on agreement with these human annotations.

For each candidate report, determine: -The count of clinically significant errors. -The count of clinically insignificant errors. Errors can fall into one of these categories: a) False report of a finding in the candidate. b) Missing a finding present in the reference. c) Misidentification of a finding's anatomic location/position. d) Misassessment of the severity of a finding. e) Mentioning a comparison that isn't in the reference. f) Omitting a comparison detailing a change from a prior study.

overall_notes: The paper introduces CREPE as an automated evaluation metric for chest X-ray report generation. It uses existing radiologist annotations from benchmark datasets to validate CREPE's performance, but does not conduct new human evaluations. The paper extensively compares CREPE against multiple automatic metrics and uses LLMs for synthetic data generation and error analysis. Extraction quality was reasonable but required normalization and removal of duplicate/redundant items.
